chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Wuhayb ibn Hafs from Abu Baseer from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said:
Our Shias are those who, when they are alone, remember Allah frequently.
ai.seo_question: What is the defining characteristic of a Shia according to this hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) identifies the core essence of Shi'ism not merely as political allegiance, but as a spiritual state of constant *dhikr* (remembrance) during solitude. This emphasizes the Shia scholarly view that true faith is manifested in the heart's private connection with the Divine, serving as the foundation for public piety and moral integrity.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Sama’at, from Wuheyb Bin Hafs, from Abu Baseer, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said: ‘
Ourasws Shias are those who when they are alone, they are doing Zikr of (mentioning) Allahazwj a lot’.
en.sarwar: 2. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama’a from Wahab ibn Hafs from abu Basir from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) has said, ‘
Our Shi’a (followers) are those who when alone speak of Allah very often.’”
